key_insight: α-stable score-based generative models match heavy-tailed targets by preserving power-law tails, and tail-index matching (α = ν) is the key condition for correct extreme-event scaling.
engineering_relevance: For applications with rare but consequential extremes—such as risk modeling, anomaly generation, or climate/finance simulation—stable dynamics can better preserve tail behavior than Brownian diffusion models.
method: Non-asymptotic p-Wasserstein convergence analysis for scale-preserving α-stable generative dynamics
Quantification of initialization, early stopping, score approximation, and time-discretization errors
Comparison against Brownian dynamics to separate global convergence from tail behavior
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence bounds, exponential decay of initialization error, and tail asymptotics showing power-law tails for stable dynamics versus light tails for Brownian dynamics.
watch_item: Tail benefits depend on correct α–ν matching; mis-specifying the stability index or using approximate scores/discretization may degrade extreme-quantile fidelity.
paper_title: From Global to Tail Convergence: Dynamics of $α$-Stable Score-Based Generative Models
